title: What If Your Plane Lost Cabin Pressure at 35,000 Feet?

scenes.text: What if your plane lost cabin pressure at 35,000 feet? You'd have under a minute to act.
Cabins are held near 8,000 feet, because the air outside is far too thin to breathe.
At 35,000 feet, useful consciousness lasts roughly 15 to 60 seconds, depending on whose table you use.
That's why oxygen masks drop automatically, once the cabin altitude passes about 14,800 feet.
Pilots then dive to lower, thicker air, where passengers can breathe normally again.
In 2016 a pilot flew at 43,000 feet without oxygen, and everyone aboard blacked out. He had started the descent first, and all survived.

description:
What if your plane lost cabin pressure at 35,000 feet?
At that height you'd have only seconds of useful consciousness, which is why the masks drop.
